content.text:
Read the shared conversation (it needed your logged-in Chrome — the public fetch returned only a login page) and audited the code against it.

**Summary:** the split "Slice / Print" button in the JusPrin header already satisfies most of the guidance in that conversation — right-edge alignment, no background dimming, hairline border, correct corner-radius math, the divider between the two halves, right-aligned muted metadata, and the full ARIA keyboard set. Four things in that list are still unfixed, and the most visible is that the dropdown touches the button with zero gap.

## Violations

**1. Zero gap between button and menu.** [HeaderControls.cpp:275](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/HeaderControls.cpp:275) positions the popup at exactly the button's bottom edge. The guidance calls for 4–8px, and specifically warns that a touching surface "reads as an expansion of the button, and the button's corner radius won't reconcile with the menu's" — which is literally the case here: the chevron half is 8px-rounded and the menu is 8px-rounded, meeting flush.

**2. No open/active state on the trigger.** `show_action_menu()` at [StatusRow.cpp:329](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/StatusRow.cpp:329) opens the popup without marking either half as active, and the button clears its own pressed state on kill-focus ([HeaderControls.cpp:80](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/HeaderControls.cpp:80)). So while the menu is open the button looks idle. The conversation lists this as fix #3 of 7.

**3. Chevron never rotates.** The icon is set to `HeaderIcon::Down` at [StatusRow.cpp:201](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/StatusRow.cpp:201) and only ever changes to the cancel X while slicing. There is no up-chevron while the menu is open.

**4. Export still uses the external-link glyph.** `HeaderIcon::Export` at [HeaderControls.cpp:57](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/HeaderControls.cpp:57) draws a box with an arrow escaping to the upper right — the "leaves the app" symbol. The conversation flags exactly this and says to use a download/save-file icon.

**5. Ellipsis convention is inconsistent** (not in the original review, found while checking it). "Print…" carries an ellipsis and correctly opens a native confirmation dialog. "Print all plates" carries none but goes through the same confirmation path at [StatusRow.cpp:446](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/StatusRow.cpp:446). One of the two is wrong.

## Minor / judgment calls

- **No open/close motion.** No animation at all; the guidance asks for 100–150ms ease-out with a 4px translate.
- **No collision handling.** The popup is positioned unconditionally with no flip or viewport clamp. Low risk for a menu dropping down from a top header, but nothing bounds it.
- **Menu row height is 40px** ([HeaderControls.cpp:127](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/HeaderControls.cpp:127)); the guidance says 32–36 for desktop. Defensible given rows carry icon + label + trailing detail.
- **Disabled items disappear rather than gray out.** "Slice all plates" is omitted from the reducer when there's one plate, and your last commit hides the whole chevron in that state. This is the opposite of the "disabled items stay visible so the menu doesn't shift between opens" rule — but it's a deliberate decision you already reasoned through, and single-plate isn't really "this action is unavailable" so much as "this concept doesn't exist here."
- **No `aria-expanded` equivalent.** Only `SetName` is set on the trigger.
- **Outside-click absorption is unverified.** The guidance wants the dismissing click swallowed rather than passed through to what's underneath. That behavior lives in wxWidgets' `wxPopupTransientWindow` and is platform-specific; I did not test it, so I can't tell you which way it goes on macOS.

## Already correct

Right-edge alignment to the trigger's outer edge; no scrim; hairline border plus the native compositor shadow with a genuinely rounded silhouette via `SetShape`; menu radius 8 with 4px container padding and 4px item radius, which matches the "item radius = menu radius − padding" formula exactly; the menu never covers the trigger; a 1px divider between the halves with independent hover on the chevron; trailing metadata ("2 sliced") right-aligned in a shared column in a muted 10pt style; and the full keyboard contract — Enter/Space opens and selects the first enabled item, Up/Down/Home/End navigate, Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger.

Want me to fix items 1–5? They're small and independent — the gap and the chevron rotation are one-liners each.

description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac; the App Store copy and other worktree builds share the bundle id, so run a re-signed copy under its own bundle id for screenshots."

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. **All five are implemented.** Changes span four files — the shared header-control widgets, the status row that builds the menu, and the shell test harness.

3. **Chevron rotation** — added `HeaderIcon::Up` and flipped it inside `paint()` via a local, deliberately *not* by mutating `m_icon`. Mutating it would call `InvalidateBestSize()` and could relayout the header on every menu open.

4. **Export icon** — replaced the arrow-escaping-a-box (external link, "leaves the app") with a down-arrow-into-a-tray at [HeaderControls.cpp:58](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/HeaderControls.cpp:58).

5. **Ellipsis** — "Print all plates" became "Print all plates…", matching "Print…". This deleted a dead branch in `action_label()` that built an inline plate count no caller ever displayed, since the menu already puts that count in the trailing detail column.

`HeaderMenu::open()` and its anchor member are now typed `HeaderButton` rather than `wxWindow`, since it has to call `set_open` on the anchor and all three call sites already passed a `HeaderButton`.

## What changed

**1. Gap.** `HeaderMenu::open()` now offsets the popup by `FromDIP(4)` below the trigger instead of placing it flush against it.

**2. Open state on the trigger.** New `HeaderButton::set_open(bool)` holds the pressed fill while the menu stands. `HeaderMenu` sets it on open and clears it on dismiss, so the flag can't leak — the menu owns it end to end. This also covers the setup chip and overflow button, which use the same menu class.

**3. Chevron rotation.** Added a `HeaderIcon::Up` glyph and flip it inside `paint()` through a local variable rather than by reassigning `m_icon`. Reassigning would call `InvalidateBestSize()` and could relayout the header every time the menu opens.

**4. Export icon.** Replaced the arrow-escaping-a-box (the external-link "leaves the app" symbol) with a down-arrow-into-a-tray.

**5. Ellipsis.** "Print all plates" became "Print all plates…". I confirmed the reason rather than assuming it: both `Print` and `Print all plates` reach the same code in [Plater.cpp:10248](src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp:10248), which opens `SelectMachineDialog` modally, so both genuinely require further input. This also deleted a dead branch in `action_label()` that built an inline plate count no caller displayed, since the menu already shows that count in its trailing column.

`HeaderMenu::open()` and its anchor member are now typed `HeaderButton` instead of `wxWindow`, since it must call `set_open` on the anchor and all three call sites already passed one.

## Verification

The harness confirms the 4px standoff numerically, that the menu item is found under its new ellipsis label, that right-edge alignment is unchanged, and that the trigger's open flag is set while the menu stands and cleared after Escape.

**Two pre-existing failures surfaced and I fixed them.** `header_split_halves_joined` and `header_action_height` failed at app startup and passed in both later evaluations. They unconditionally measured the chevron half's position and height, but the previous commit — 575ee93aae, "Hide the header print-action chevron when its menu is empty" — made that half hidden for a single unsliced plate, which is exactly the startup state. Nothing in my diff touches widget geometry, which is precisely why the chevron flip goes through a paint-time local. I made those checks branch on visibility and added `header_lone_action_precedes_overflow` for the hidden case; the clean run confirms the diagnosis.

## One gap you should know about

Your instinct is right, and it's actually two separate issues stacked on top of each other. The border you're seeing is a *focus ring*, not a menu highlight — and it's being drawn on mouse-open, which isn't conventional either.

## Issue 1: the visual treatment is the wrong shape

The code has two different ways of showing "this row is active." Hover fills the row with a tinted background ([HeaderControls.cpp:146](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/HeaderControls.cpp:146)), but keyboard selection draws a 2px outlined rounded rectangle ([HeaderControls.cpp:196](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/HeaderControls.cpp:196)) — the same treatment the header buttons use for keyboard focus:

```cpp
if (HasFocus() || m_menu_selected) {
    gc->SetBrush(*wxTRANSPARENT_BRUSH); gc->SetPen(wxPen(p.border_focus,FromDIP(2)));
```

So one concept has two visual languages. Worse, the auto-selected row on open gets the ring with *no* fill, because the mouse isn't over it — which is exactly the state in your screenshot. Menus conventionally indicate the active row with a filled background; an outlined box around a row reads as a text field or a focused button, which is why it looks foreign to you.

## Issue 2: pre-selecting on a mouse click isn't conventional

`HeaderMenu::open()` unconditionally selects the first enabled item ([HeaderControls.cpp:283](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/HeaderControls.cpp:283)), regardless of how the menu was opened. The convention — confirmed in the W3C ARIA Authoring Practices discussion — is that focus stays on the button when the menu is opened by mouse, and moves to the first item only when opened by keyboard. macOS native menus behave this way too: nothing is highlighted until you hover or press an arrow key.

There *is* a real reason the code does this, noted in a comment right there: the popup owns its own keyboard selection because Cocoa delivers keys to the popup without assigning focus to a child view. But it doesn't need a pre-selected item to work — the arrow-key handler already starts from index −1 and lands on the first item on the first Down press, and Enter with nothing selected does nothing. So dropping the pre-selection on mouse-open costs nothing functionally.

## What I'd change

1. **Render menu selection as a fill**, the same tint hover already uses, and stop drawing the focus ring on menu rows. One visual language for one concept.
2. **Pre-select only when the menu was opened from the keyboard.** This needs `HeaderButton` to record whether its last activation came from Return/Space rather than a click, and `open()` to read that — a small addition, since `activate()` is already the single funnel for both paths.

Keeping the keyboard case is worth it: a keyboard user who opens the menu with no row highlighted has no visible starting point, and that's a genuine accessibility regression rather than a style preference.

Want me to make both changes? It's contained to the two files I already touched, and I can extend the harness to assert that a mouse-opened menu starts with nothing selected while a keyboard-opened one starts on the first enabled row.

git commit -F - <<'EOF'
Align the header print dropdown with menu conventions

The split print button in the JusPrin header diverged from how desktop
menus behave in several ways at once. The menu surface sat flush against
the button, so it read as an extension of the button rather than a
separate surface, and the two 8px corner radii met with nothing between
them. The trigger gave no sign it was active: neither half changed while
its menu stood open, and the chevron kept pointing down. Export used an
arrow escaping a box, which means "leaves the app" rather than "writes a
file". And "Print all plates" carried no ellipsis even though it opens
SelectMachineDialog exactly as the menu's "Print..." does.

The menu now stands off the trigger by 4px. HeaderButton gains set_open,
which HeaderMenu sets for the lifetime of the popup and clears on
dismiss; an open trigger holds its pressed fill, and a down chevron is
painted as an up chevron. That flip reads m_icon at paint time instead
of reassigning it, so the button's best size never changes and the
header does not relayout when a menu opens. Export draws a download
tray. action_label returns "Print all plates..." and no longer builds an
inline plate count that no caller displayed, since the menu already
places that count in its trailing column.

Menu rows also indicated selection two different ways: hover filled the
row while keyboard selection drew the 2px focus ring that header buttons
use, and the ring is what a row got when the menu opened. Selection is
now a fill in both cases, and menu rows never paint a focus ring at all
-- the popup owns selection for the whole list, so a row holding native
focus after Popup() is an artifact rather than a selected row. Following
the ARIA menu-button pattern, only a keyboard-opened menu starts on its
first row; a mouse-opened one highlights nothing until the pointer or an
arrow key picks one. Arrow keys work from either state, with Up wrapping
to the last row when nothing is selected yet.

The shell harness asserts the 4px standoff, that the trigger is marked
open while the menu stands and cleared after Escape, and that the two
open paths differ. Two of its header checks measured the chevron half
unconditionally and had been failing since that half became hidden for a
single unsliced plate; they now branch on visibility. Verified live:
mouse-opened menu with no highlight, keyboard-opened menu filling its
first row, up chevron and darker trigger while open, download glyph on
Export.
EOF
